audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Ornn Levels 2 and 3 while the prose beneath them said the opposite ('he free-trades while I last-hit', 'he edges level 3').
audit.why: Mirror (garen__ornn) rewrote the chart as one group: Levels 1 through 4-5 to Garen, Level 6 to Ornn. Packet chart agrees on rows 0-2 and row 4. 49.5% over 4218 games matches a losing early, winning mid.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 flip to Garen (4/10 from your side), row 4 flips to Ornn; rows 5-6 already Ornn. Proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1]/[2]/[3].why all described Ornn-favoured stages that the chart no longer supports, and named no cooldowns.
audit.why: Courage is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s and Decisive Strike is a flat 8s — those are the numbers that decide when you can walk up.
audit.corrected: Rewrote phases[1].why, phases[2].why, phases[3].why and breakdown.cooldowns with the real durations.

audit.whatIsWrong: Decisive Strike was never identified as an auto-attack reset, so the advice keyed off the cast instead of the wind-up.
audit.why: Garen Q carries the autoReset flag alongside silence and slow; the reset is the burst tell. Listed in missingInteractions (autoreset-burst-tell).
audit.corrected: Written into report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns; Courage restated as shield plus tenacity in dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole content layer for this matchup is written in first person ('I have no shield', 'my E-Q burst') instead of the second-person voice used everywhere else.
audit.why: The approved quality bar is the user's second-person voice.
audit.corrected: Fixed in whys[0] and whys[3]; the rest of the first-person lines flagged for a voice pass rather than churned inside the length band.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Courage's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.

edits.after: - Garen Courage: 22s at rank 1, 12s maxed — shield plus tenacity, so bait it before you commit. - Decisive Strike: 8s auto reset that silences — the wind-up is your cue to step back. - Call of the Forge God: 140s.
